DRAFT CRITIQUE (architecture-decisions gate, 2026-08-14). The proposed ADR 0096, ADR 0095 partial-supersession banner, ADR index/number marker, and transitional docs/architecture.md update are drafted locally; no implementation or test routing changed.

1. Claims lacking research citations: none outstanding. All five OSS links were HTTP-validated at their pinned SHAs; the Rust citation was corrected from the standalone-guide repository to rust-lang/rust/src/doc/rustc-dev-guide at 059bf4a660dd. Timing and assertion-map claims cite run 31798375024 and umbrella ticket 4f50-b1f2-78af-4326.
2. Internal inconsistencies: none outstanding after correction. docs/architecture.md now says ADR 0095 every-assertion-live routing remains current until the separate implementation lands, rather than falsely describing the proposed boundary as already active. ADR 0096 is Status: Proposed and carries Superseded by: N/A.
3. Missing constraints: the draft now states the existing external workflow is Ubuntu-only and requires the implementation to add an Ubuntu+macOS Pandoc matrix. It explicitly accepts weekly detection delay and lower-cadence runner contention. It also requires any future fixture-changing Gerrit change to run External Integration Tests against the exact proposed ref via a temporary GitHub mirror branch before those bytes become the new compatibility baseline. No unresolved constraint remains.
4. Conflicts with documented decisions: only ADR 0095 conflicts. The same change marks exactly its every-conversion-assertion-live clause partially superseded and states every production renderer, pin, safety, platform, degradation, immutability, and cutover decision remains authoritative. No other ADR conflict was found.

Local draft guards already pass: gen_adr_index.py --check, check_adr_numbers.py, check_docs_index.py, git diff --check. Per the mandatory lifecycle, HOLD is blocked until the operator explicitly confirms this draft critique.
